title: People’s Mañanera November 13
author: Pedro Gellert
content:
_Every day, President Claudia Sheinbaum gives a morning presidential press
conference and Mexico Solidarity Media posts English language summaries,
translated by Mexico Solidarity 's Pedro Gellert. Previous press conference
summaries are available [here](https://mexicosolidarity.com/mananera/)._

**Sheinbaum Congratulates AMLO on His 73rd Birthday  
** “We send our regards to President López Obrador; from here we send our
love, appreciation, and admiration—always,” Claudia Sheinbaum said as she
congratulated the founder of the Fourth Transformation on his birthday.

**Mexico Breaks Five Historic Records in Tourism  
** From January through September, Mexico welcomed 74.9 million international
travelers, whose spending totaled almost US$26.10 billion. The country’s ports
received 9 million cruise passengers, who boosted local commerce and
handicrafts.

**INDEP Turns Recovered Assets into Social Well-Being, Raising Over 407
Million Pesos (US$21.95 Million) and Funding 56 Social Projects  
** “They asked me to build a conservatory,” the President recalled, and,
fulfilling her commitment, she issued instructions to donate 40.2 million
pesos (US$2.17 million) recovered by the Institute for Returning Stolen Assets
to the People (INDEP) to the Tultepec Conservatory of Music and Cultural
Center, which will serve 3,500 students.

**Sheinbaum Calls for Review of INE Contracts Amid Allegations Against Somos
Leaders  
** In light of two investigations into alleged irregularities for more than
563 million pesos (US$30.37 million) involving former National Electoral
Institute (INE) officials who are now with the Somos political party,
Sheinbaum asked the Federal Superior Audit Office (ASF) to review INE and
Local Public Electoral Bodies’ (OPLE) contracts for electoral materials from
2014 to 2025 and for the Federal Attorney General’s Office (FGR) to intervene
if warranted. In addition, the President described huge severance payments of
up to 13 million pesos (US$700,000) to former INE officials as immoral.
